---
title: "About"
---

digital.eee began with the [Verilog Crash Course](https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph/pages/verilogCrashCourse/index.html), which I originally wrote and distributed through UVLe, the university’s online learning management system. When we decided to expand the course with exercises and assessments, we needed a repository to bring those materials together. Then we imagined students writing and simulating Verilog directly on the course webpage. That idea called for a website, and digital.eee took shape. In late 2025, Lawrence Roman Quizon designed and implemented the hosting infrastructure that made it possible.

By 2026, we had begun expanding the site with interactive simulators to accompany the digital design courses I care about. Much of that work grew out of frustration. I kept relying on slide animations and doodles to explain concepts that students could understand much more easily if they could see them in action. These were fundamental digital design concepts, yet I could not find online tools that visualized them in quite the way I wanted to teach them. So I started developing those tools and bringing them together here.

I currently create most of the site’s content. The materials and simulators reflect my taste in teaching: intuitive, highly visual, and deliberately generous with guidance. I want students to follow what happens, explore why it happens, and work through the details at their own pace.

The site continues to evolve rapidly as we—and, much of the time, I—develop more content. Behind that work is a dream of democratizing digital design education: making the explanations and tools I wish I had more accessible to anyone who wants to learn.
